reviewStandard: Scientific identity, current controlled identifiers, primary scientific references, non-diagnostic framing, literal generation-call provenance, and original-resolution visual-count reconciliation are recorded. assets.scientificFinding: NCBI recognizes Bifidobacteriaceae as current family NCBITaxon:31953. Comparative genomics and current descendant records support a deliberately selective family-level plate spanning bifid or tapered rods, short rods, small pleomorphic coccobacillary forms, and rudimentary branching. The plate does not claim that these forms exhaust or diagnose the family, and relative scale is illustrative.
assets.visualReview: Five separated morphology groupings contain eight cellular bodies: one clean Y-shaped bifid body, two long tapered rods, two short blunt rods, two small ovoid coccobacillary bodies, and one short irregular body with a shallow integral branch. No appendages, spores, capsule halos, host materials, text, labels, scale bar, watermark, crowding, or edge clipping are visible.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI recognizes Bifidobacterium adolescentis as current species NCBITaxon:1680. The type-strain record supports Gram-positive anaerobic rods, while original electron-microscopy work documents intrinsic bifid and Y-shaped morphology without requiring a stress treatment. The reconstruction does not assert appendages, spores, or diagnostic exclusivity.

All branches are substantial cell-body continuations rather than hairs. No appendages, spores, capsule halos, host materials, text, labels, scale bar, watermark, crowding, or edge clipping are visible.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI recognizes Bifidobacterium bifidum as current species NCBITaxon:1681. The DSMZ type-strain record supports rod morphology, and the primary Poupard/Husain/Norris study describes the normal form as a curved rod or bifid form while distinguishing nutrition-associated highly branched forms. The restrained replacement therefore combines curved and tapered rods with one subtle true bifid body without implying universal branching or diagnostic exclusivity.
assets.visualReview: Six separated groupings contain seven cellular bodies: five singles comprising three gently curved or irregular tapered rods, one mildly clubbed curved rod, and one true bifid body with a short smooth integral Y end, plus a touching two-cell pair of curved tapered rods. The Y branches are substantial continuations of the cell body rather than hairs. No appendages, spores, capsule halos, host materials, text, labels, scale bar, watermark, crowding, or edge clipping are visible.

outputAudit.observedSubjectDescription: Seven cellular bodies in six visual groupings: five singles including curved, tapered, mildly clubbed, and one true bifid Y-ended form, plus one touching pair of two curved tapered rods.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI recognizes Bifidobacterium breve as current species NCBITaxon:1685. The type-strain record supports Gram-positive anaerobic rods. Original electron-microscopy work found predominantly rod-shaped control cells and bifid morphology under selected amino-acid conditions, so this canonical plate deliberately depicts the restrained unstressed rod treatment rather than implying that branching is universal.

The cells show restrained variation from compact to moderately elongated, with rounded ends and no Y forms. No appendages, spores, capsule halos, host materials, text, labels, scale bar, watermark, crowding, or edge clipping are visible.

assets.reason: NCBI Taxonomy assigns NCBITaxon:1682 to the current subspecies Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis and records Bifidobacterium infantis as its basionym. Taxonomic studies published in 2002 and 2008 unified the former species with B. longum and established the current subspecies combination, while LPSN and the DSMZ type-strain record use that current name. The WikiBiome route overview describes the current subspecies, but its canonical route and title still assert the historical species combination.
assets.requiredResolution: Rename or redirect the canonical route to a current-name bifidobacterium-longum-subsp-infantis record keyed to NCBITaxon:1682, or explicitly reframe the existing route as a historical or common-name alias whose canonical subject and structured metadata are Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis.
assets.routingImpact: The obsolete route has no generated draft, registry record, master, derivative, review approval, or image-sitemap entry. After control integrates the canonical identity change and regenerates the deterministic register, bifidobacterium-longum-subsp-infantis enters the microorganism queue as uncovered at the corresponding eligible position; batch 007 itself contains no substitution.
assets.resolution: Control retired the obsolete species-form route and established a permanent 308 alias to the current canonical Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis record.

excludedIdentityReferences.reason: This is a strain-level record and must not be used as the controlled identity for the canonical subspecies subject.
